incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 — gpu-driver-reset-high-rate detected in us-west-2 (autoscale pool). Paging oncall.

Maya: observed repeated driver resets on three hosts, Xid 79 & 102 spikes. Affected inference pods returning 500s and some customers seeing degraded p99 latency.

David: oncall here, joining. Which hosts?

Maya: host ids: gpu-usw2-03, gpu-usw2-07, gpu-usw2-11. Last ~20 mins, resets every ~2-10m on those nodes.

Ivan: grabbing logs now. dmesg tail shows:```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=4123, p=python3, smr=0x4
[ 12346.123456] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: driver reset
[ 12346.123459] irq 64: no irq handler for vector
```

Kira: container logs show a mix of cuda errors and OOM kills for the transformer-worker container around the same timestamp. Looks like the driver reset causes process requeues -> memory spike -> oom.

Elena: started rolling check: any recent kernel or driver pushes in the region?

deploy-bot: Deploys: No driver/kernel packages pushed in last 24h. No recent runtime changes.

Maya: telemetry: GPU ECC correctable errors tick up just before the reset on two hosts. Might be thermal/ECC scrubbing noise.

ops-sre: tagging this as possible hardware-induced resets vs driver bug. Let's triage with mitigation path: 1) move inference traffic off the three hosts; 2) reduce concurrency (batch size) for the model to lower memory pressure; 3) if spread continues, cordon + drain nodes and restart GPU services.

David: doing step 1 — updating smart-routing to avoid these hosts. @ops-sre please confirm drain order.

ops-sre: prefer cordon gpu-usw2-11 first (highest reset rate), then 03, then 07. Use `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and mark nodes out of LB.

Maya: command I ran on gpu-usw2-11:```
kubectl cordon gpu-usw2-11
kubectl drain gpu-usw2-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=5m
```

Maya: pods evicted, traffic shifted. p99 latency for the impacted customer dropped from 1.2s -> 420ms after routing change.

Ivan: seeing residual retries from long in-flight requests; some jobs hit container OOM after retry backoff. Recommend lowering model worker concurrency globally for the AK release channel: set WORKER_CONCURRENCY=2 temporarily.

Kira: rolling config change to reduce concurrency on the model pool. Applying canary to 10% first.

deploy-bot: Config update posted. Canary applied to model-pool-canary. No errors so far.

Elena: hardware check — IPMI shows one of the DIMMs on gpu-usw2-07 with corrected ECC spikes but no uncorrectable errors. Temp sensors normal. Suggest we keep nodes cordoned and engage hardware team for deeper scrub.

David: agreed. I'll do an oncall handoff update to infra+hw teams. Need customer comms? Which customers impacted?

Maya: two paying customers (acct-770 and acct-199) saw 5-10% of requests retried with increased latency. Both are on Standard tier. No data exfiltration.

David: writing short bridge note and escalation to account reps.

David: @ops-sre, plan of record for next 2 hours: maintain routing exclusion, keep affected nodes cordoned, hardware diagnostics (memtest + ECC scrub), if driver resets continue after HW check, try driver rollback to previous stable package on a single node as canary.

ops-sre: noted. Also recommend tuning host-level NVregWatchdogTimeout and set `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset` not available; will use short OS reboot if reset loop continues.

Maya: quick mitigation checklist I used:```
# shift traffic
PATCH /routing/pools/model-usw2 exclude [gpu-usw2-03,gpu-usw2-07,gpu-usw2-11]
# reduce in-pod concurrency
kubectl set env deploy/model-worker WORKER_CONCURRENCY=2 -n inference
# cordon & drain nodes in order
```

Ivan: assigning ticket INF-5421 for follow-up (hardware/driver deep-dive). Adding logs and timelines.

Kira: after canary change to concurrency=2, model error rates dropped 60% in the canary group. Proceeding to full rollout.

Maya: full rollout complete. Metrics look stable, no new Xid events in the last 8 minutes on remaining nodes.

ops-sre: hardware team scheduled on-site check for gpu-usw2-07 tomorrow. For now keep nodes cordoned until memtest completes.

Elena: suggest enabling GPU ECC scrubbing on those hosts and monitoring for correctable error stabilization.

David: summarizing for handoff:
- Incident: intermittent GPU driver resets (Xid 79/102) in us-west-2 causing inference 500s and OOMs due to retry/memory storm.
- Mitigation: routed traffic away from affected hosts, reduced worker concurrency (WORKER_CONCURRENCY=2), drained & cordoned 3 nodes, rolling config canary -> full rollout.
- Impact: two Standard-tier customers saw elevated p99 and retries; no data loss.
- Next steps: hardware memtest + ECC scrub, keep nodes cordoned, ticket INF-5421 assigned, consider driver rollback if resets persist after hardware check.

David: handing over to night oncall @Maya (followup) and infra lead @Ivan. Please escalate if resets return or if memtest shows UCEs.

Maya: will monitor and post updates. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Oncall handoff created: handoff_ts=2881234602, owner=Maya, severity=P1, followups=[INF-5421].

Elena: leaving SANITY checklist in INF-5421: attach `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi --query`, container oom logs, per-node ECC counters, and routing patch diff.

Ivan: collecting artifacts now and will update ticket.

(End of thread)
